 BELOIT — Two children died in a house fire early Sunday morning in the 1000 block of Hinsdale Avenue.
 Beloit Fire Department crews were called to the fire at about 3:47 a.m.
 When the first responding firefighters arrived, the entire second floor was fully involved in smoke and flame, said Beloit Fire Chief Todd Farley.
 “The first responding crew did a transitional attack,” Farley said, noting firefighters attacked the fire from the exterior. “Ladders then were extended to the second floor window to rescue the victims inside.”
 Firefighters found a 7-year-old girl and a 13-year-old boy who were deceased. The mother survived and was taken from the home. The father was not home at the time of the fire.
 The house, which was showing extensive first and second floor damage, is considered a total loss, Farley said.
 The cause of the fire still is the subject of investigation. The Beloit Fire Department, State Fire Marshall, Beloit Police Department and Rock County Medical Examiner’s Office are investigating the incident.
 Farley said the tragic fire is a reminder to everyone to make sure they have smoke detectors and to continue to make sure they are in good working order. He said the investigation is in its early stages and he doesn’t know if there were smoke detectors in the house, but he wanted to stress the importance of having smoke detectors.
 “Smoke detectors save lives. Anyone who can’t afford them, we (the fire department) have them available for residents,” he said. “Remember to change batteries twice a year at the time of daylight savings time.”
